title: Pattern matching — remember
rememberThis: is and switch expressions are the two hosts for patterns; declaration patterns also introduce a variable in scope only when the match succeeds.
The compiler warns on unreachable arms and on missing cases; _ is the discard that silences exhaustiveness by matching everything left.
Relational patterns compare to constants; combine them with and/or/not, not with && inside the pattern.
with on a record copies and sets named properties; it does not mutate the original. Classes need a clone story of their own.
Auth and LTI branching belongs in a switch expression over a closed set of providers, not in a chain of magic strings scattered across controllers — this track stays in the language, not ASP.NET.
bullets: Expression-bodied members are => on methods, properties, constructors, and indexers; they are not a different runtime.
List patterns plus .. slice are the right tool for ragged CSV rows.
null is a constant pattern; is not null is the logical not of that constant.

rows.label: switch statement vs expression
rows.value: Statement: labels, fall-through forbidden except empty case. Expression: arms return a value, must be exhaustive.

rows.value: { Kind: "lti", Version: "1.3" } matches those properties; nested patterns go inside.

rows.value: var next = current with { ExpiresAt = utc }; records and some structs with copy constructors.
